Article Title: 80% of India’s insurance buying journey now happens online, Google-McKinsey report claims
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

Why Indians are buying insurance online

“The DICA consumer highlights that purchasing insurance in India is an intricate journey where no single touchpoint or advisor operates in isolation.

When the digital ecosystem directly influences more than 40% of all insurance purchases the online shortlist becomes an important decisive factor. Closing the gap between a consumer's digital evaluation and their offline advisory experience is now the biggest lever for insurance penetration and value creation.

”

Non-metro consumers and salaried professionals lead online research

AI search and YouTube influence insurance decisions

Why insurance buyers still need human assistance

“The emergence of the

DICA consumers

will boost awareness and accessibility in the insurance sector. For insurers, enabling this journey seamlessly across their omnichannel distribution network, like advisors, websites, mobile apps and other digital platforms, can help in building consumer confidence and trust, and thereby increase insurance penetration in India.”

“The future of insurance distribution will not be defined by where customers buy, but by how effectively we connect digital discovery with trusted advice.

When more than 40% of policies are already digitally influenced, the industry's next growth opportunity lies in converting informed intent into meaningful protection.”

Insurance buying in India is increasingly shifting towards online. According to a new study by Google , with McKinsey & Company as its knowledge partner, nearly 80% of India's insurance buying journey now happens online, with consumers using search engines and videos to research policies before approaching an advisor. The report also found that digital research directly influences 40% of health and life insurance sales.‘Decoding the DICA Consumer’ study shows an expanding category of purchasers who shop for insurance providers and filter options online before turning to human assistance to complete the purchase. The findings indicate that digital platforms are influencing insurance decisions, but customers still value a human adviser's input on policy wording, cover, and future financial security.The report identifies these consumers as Digitally Influenced, Closed with Assistance (DICA) buyers. They research policies online, shortlist insurers and then approach advisors to validate their choices and understand policy details.Siddharth Shekar, Director, Google India, said,The report found that 78% of consumers narrow their choices to two or three insurance brands online before speaking to an advisor. More than 50% of consumers continue to prefer their original online shortlist even after consulting an agent.The findings indicate that advisors increasingly need to answer specific questions about coverage, policy exclusions, and service support rather than introduce buyers to insurance brands from scratch.Online insurance research is not limited to consumers in metropolitan cities. According to the study, consumers in leading non-metro cities conduct roughly twice as much online research before purchasing a policy compared with the national average.Salaried professionals aged 25–35 represent the largest demographic driving this digital research. The group also shows higher engagement with comparison tools and policy explainers across age groups.The report calls on insurers to involve consumers at the research stage when they're considering options, rather than only through traditional sales channels.AI-powered search tools and video content are helping consumers understand insurance products. The study found that longer queries account for 18% of insurance searches on Google, reflecting demand for information about specific coverage requirements and complicated policy terms.It also found that 41% of users use AI Overviews to compare options and establish their coverage requirements before approaching an insurer.Video is another important part of the buying journey. Approximately 60% of online insurance researchers use videos during their research, while insurance-related content on YouTube crossed 2.5 billion views in India over the past year. More than 15% of these views occurred on YouTube Connected TV, suggesting insurance research can also involve discussions among household members.Meanwhile, insurance mobile apps are seeing increased engagement for routine activities such as tracking policies and managing claims.Despite the shift towards online research, the study found that fewer than 30% of buyers are comfortable purchasing high-value insurance policies entirely through digital checkout processes.Consumers still seek help understanding policy exclusions, confirming long-term financial security, and getting support during hospital claims. However, the transition from online research to offline sales is not always seamless.More than 40% of buyers said they were frustrated by having to repeat their requirements after being contacted as new leads. More than a third also cited generic sales scripts that did not reflect their specific needs.The report found that offline insurance purchases influenced by online research generate policy premiums approximately 40% higher than traditional sales.Parthanil Ghosh, Managing Director and CEO, HDFC ERGO General Insurance, said,Sumit Madan, Managing Director and CEO, Axis Max Life Insurance, said,The study's findings are based on a survey of 1,039 insurance consumers; aggregated, masked lead-to-conversion analysis across life and health insurers; interviews with industry advisors and distribution platforms; and insights from Google and McKinsey.
Article Summary: Nearly 80% of India's insurance buying journey now happens online. Digital research directly influences 40% of health and life insurance sales. Digital platforms are influencing insurance decisions, but customers still value a human adviser's input on policy wording, cover, and future financial security.

Article Title: When AI valuations correct, India’s case for AI diffusion gets strong
Article Text:
There is No Set Timeline for ‘AGI’ or Generative AI

Industrial AI Policy Push is not a Zero-Sum Game for Public and Private Ecosystems in India

By: Abhivardhan, Managing Partner, Indic Pacific, Sunil Khemka, Program Chair, IEEE Chicago and Technical Convenor (AI & OSS),

, Sanad Arora, Chief Innovation Lead, Indian Society of Artificial Intelligence and Law

Recently, a notable remark from within India’s economic policy establishment observed that if AI-related valuations are subject to market corrections in the advanced economies, then it might be positive for capital inflows in the context of India. His remark should be seen in conjunction with the caution raised in an economic forum that there exists an AI bubble in the US. Naturally, such statements may be seen as defeatist in some ways. However, considering the mainstreaming of AI diffusion across some business-to-business and many business-to-consumer ecosystems, even if the pace is varied across industries, these remarks could make a genuine and unique case of AI Diffusion in late-industrial states, like India.For instance, economists have warned that AI diffusion strains mid-sized enterprises. While some of the “AI Economists” and few other traditional economists argue that the risk of labour or talent replacement remains impeccably high, the real pressure stems from expanding capital disparity. This could be driven by how private equity firms are investing in certain AI firms who then collaborate with certain data rights holders and content publishers.In China, for instance, hedge funds were critical in backing DeepSeek’s success and growth. However, the success of AI labs like DeepSeek has pushed an economically viable chance for the rest of the world including India to pursue alternative options. However, the apocalyptic doom narratives coming from the US exploit actual tension that mid-size firms and startups face. That actual tension, unfortunately, is structural, where mid-market firms are needed to navigate bloated enterprise software costs while maintaining essential human oversight, which in addition - is an unavoidable investment. Nevertheless, as low-cost open models can reduce costs, the vector of “moat” for startups and mid-sized firms unintentionally returns to fundamental research & development, which might explain why AI diffusion is certainly not a lost cause for late industrial states.For late industrial states like India, a more explicit claim has been made that they lack concentrated private equity capital to build proprietary trillion-parameter models like two major AI labs. While from a general R&D perspective it is an issue and one may argue how private and public functionaries support AI and DeepTech initiatives, the infusion of capital should be furthered in those segments and assets, which create a cycle of successive counterparts of the same segments. For instance, a chip design firm in India was acquired by foreign VCs and some commentators argued that it was hurting India’s semiconductor industry and technological sovereignty. Contrary to how they assume, this acquisition made a clear economic case of investing in more Indian talent and resources within India to build more such firms, since the semiconductor economy globally is an interconnected web. However, it does not imply that no sovereign AI ecosystems can be enabled in India at all. Unfortunately, policy reports and sections of a commentariat who argue for and against the “sovereign AI” idea treat the idea as some zero-sum game. The reason they make such flawed assumptions is because they conflate building trillion-parameter models and massive data centres as a measure of geostrategic competition. Since most facets of geostrategic competition are seen as rather zero-sum games, the conflated assumption is cast upon in the case of AI as well. This begs us to ask whether in the pyramid of various “layers” of the AI ecosystem, Indian entities are bound to remain interdependent on all or any layers.Now, one has to understand why this is important. There has been a concerted attempt for years by philosophers, economists and even the prominent AI labs to push the AI doom narrative from a very cut-throat angle of geostrategic competition. It could have made sense to an extent considering the schools of thought around US-China relations that people have developed, and how they particularly look at the economics and certain AI-enabled risks. However, since most of the AI safety discourse focuses on models, and pushes a narrative of AI-associative organised chaos. For instance, Daniel Kokotajlo had created a timeline in a paper called AI 2027, as per which he made technical predictions about the arrival of artificial general intelligence (AGI). While the four major labs kind of diverge on the timelines of AGI, the AI 2027 hypothesis fell flat, since the eagerness to suggest an AGI arrival timeline lacked technical clarity and did not take into account the limitations of the transformers-language models ecosystem.Despite the backlash against AI 2027, various theorists, economists and tech professionals keep proposing timelines around AGI, which centered too much around this US-China competition. Unfortunately, they conflate the persistent promotion of a discourse around US-China AI & compute competition with a rigorous analysis of actual AI evolution & industrial diffusion timelines, which makes no sense.If we look at India’s industrial AI ecosystem developments, there have been enough developments in the semiconductor and electronics industries which show a positive trend. Data centers is another AI ecosystem industry category which is having a calibrative moment nationwide beyond the efforts in Vizag. This leaves us with AI talent, demand issues around AI products & services and AI technical architecture costs beyond cloud / storage and compute. The aftermath of the AI Impact Summit 2026 was interesting for the Indian tech ecosystem, since realisation loomed among India’s startup founders and managers that building AI in India while has challenges around data, funds, and even working culture, emulating a zero-sum approach that is usually pushed in the Silicon Valley is not helpful, irrespective of whether an AI startup intends to sell their products and services in India or beyond. India has immense talent in the AI and analytics space as well as in non-AI industrial sectors, across service & manufacturing sectors whose potential remains untapped, and unfortunately, trapped. In fact, there is a “considerable disconnect in awardees, grants, and the promise vs. delivery of public benefit” as pointed out by economic development specialist Smita Srinivas. This disconnect, often reflects in distorting which technical research and non-AI technical talent to invest in, how to ensure market trust, examining whether a for-profit approach or a not-for-profit approach is logistically sensible for the AI and DeepTech startups building in India. The Indian AI ecosystem must realise that any AI research and diffusion push cannot be treated as a zero-sum game, when in advanced economies, AI diffusion and evolution cycles are conflated with a geostrategic, zero-sum angle of AI diffusion, which might make some of these advanced economies, in WENA countries, especially in North America, lonelier, especially around data, talent & research cooperation. In fact, the shift from traditional SaaS and BPO-like AI delivery models toward the intersection of AI-enabled industrial engineering can also show new horizons. Therefore, the infusion of software engineers and domain specialists can pivot new industry segmentations and opportunities, which is shown by countries like Japan, in their approach towards cooperative AI. It is high time these market distortions are avoided.
Article Summary: Industrial AI Policy Push is not a Zero-Sum Game for Public and Private Ecosystems in India. There is No Set Timeline for ‘AGI’ or Generative AI. There has been a concerted attempt for years by philosophers, economists and even prominent AI labs to push the AI doom narrative.

Article Title: Microsoft’s next-generation Xbox may launch after 2028: Here is how much it may cost
Article Text:
Microsoft Project Helix (Representational image)

New leadership and hardware realities

What is Microsoft's Project ‘ Xbox Helix ’

Gamers must brace for expensive computing hardware over the next few years, specifically for flagship consoles. According to a report by Fortune, internal Microsoft estimates project that the next-generation Xbox could cost between $1,200 and $1,800. On top of the potential pricing spike, the system may not hit store shelves until 2028. Notably, at an $1,800 ceiling, the upcoming console would cost nearly four times as much as its predecessor did at launch. This comes as industry rumours suggest Sony’s anticipated PlayStation 6 could also climb upwards of $1,000.The price and launch timeline come at a time when Microsoft’s gaming division is undergoing a period of major restructuring, marked by additional workforce layoffs and the appointment of Asha Sharma as the new chief executive officer (CEO) of Xbox. Sharma has laid out targets for the brand, including scaling Xbox into a billion-player-a-day platform.Meanwhile, persistent global hardware inflation is challenging the standard business model. Microsoft itself believes it’s no longer feasible to develop a high-performance machine that boasts flagship capabilities and fits in the traditional consumer-friendly price tags.For players seeking a more wallet-friendly entry point, Microsoft may offer an alternative ahead of its flagship living-room hardware.Sharma told Fortune that an official next-generation Xbox handheld is planned for release in time for the holiday 2027 shopping season.While launching the portable device in late 2027 gives global component volatility some breathing room, major technology manufacturers widely anticipate that industry-wide memory shortages will linger well into 2028.The persistent supply snags present a major hurdle for the upcoming home console, codenamed Xbox Helix. Microsoft will need to lock down final architectural choices and commit to massive component orders ahead of high-volume mass production – an operational milestone anticipated for late 2027 or early 2028. The surging costs of raw silicon, advanced memory modules and specialised fabrication account directly for the eye-watering estimates.While cutting-edge exclusives and next-generation processing muscle will inevitably attract dedicated early adopters, the prospect of a console priced past $1,500 introduces steep commercial risks.
Article Summary: Microsoft's next-generation Xbox could cost as much as $1,800. The system may not hit store shelves until 2028. The price and launch timeline come at a time when Microsoft’s gaming division is undergoing a period of major restructuring, marked by additional workforce layoffs.

Article Title: Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 sees surge in home upgrades, demand grows beyond metros
Article Text: Home upgrades have emerged as one of the biggest shopping trends during the ongoing Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, with shopping volumes growing more than threefold as consumers invest in kitchen appliances, smart home products, entertainment devices and large household appliances ahead of Diwali.According to Amazon India, growth is increasingly being driven by smaller cities, with non-metro markets accounting for more than 60% of shopping volumes and expanding at twice the rate of metro cities. Cities such as Lucknow, Jaipur, Patna, Guwahati, Coimbatore, Nagpur, Indore and Kochi are leading demand, as customers increasingly explore new product categories and upgrade to premium appliances.Commenting on the trend, Aman Deep Lohan, Director, Home, Kitchen and Outdoors at Amazon India, said consumers are showing growing confidence in upgrading their homes with technology-focused products, while affordability options such as no-cost EMI, exchange offers and instant bank discounts are helping shoppers make larger purchases.According to the company, AI-powered cooking appliances, robotic vacuum cleaners, air purifiers and connected lighting products are among the key categories witnessing increased demand during the festive sale.Amazon also highlighted the role of its AI shopping assistant Rufus, which allows customers to search for products using natural language queries in multiple Indian languages, including Hinglish.Air fryers, refrigerators and dishwashers see strong growthThe company said the kitchen appliances category is currently growing at 3.4 times its average daily pace, with smart and small appliances recording growth of 4.5 times. Air fryers have emerged among the fastest-growing products, operating at 7.5 times their average-day sales pace, while ovens are growing at 5.2 times. Brands such as Philips and SharkNinja have reported growth of more than seven times compared with regular sales periods. Premium refrigerators are also witnessing strong traction. Refrigerators with capacities above 300 litres are selling at 34 times their average-day pace, led by frost-free and side-by-side models from Samsung, LG, Haier and Bosch. Amazon said the Samsung 653-litre AI-enabled side-by-side refrigerator is operating at 33 times its average-day pace.Other lifestyle-oriented kitchen categories are gaining momentum as well, with dishwashers growing sevenfold and chimneys sixfold compared with normal sales levels.Smart TVs, robotic cleaners and connected lighting gain popularityThe living room category is also seeing significant upgrades as consumers opt for larger screens and connected devices. According to Amazon, home entertainment products, including smart TVs and speakers, are running at 37 times their average-day sales pace, with smart TVs accounting for nearly 65% of the category's growth.Brands including Samsung, Xiaomi and TCL have collectively grown 56 times compared with average sales levels, while Indian brand Lumio recorded a 42-fold increase. Robotic vacuum cleaners are another fast-growing category, with sales running at 9.2 times normal levels. Brands such as Ecovacs and Dreame are among the key beneficiaries of this trend. Demand for air purifiers has increased 5.2 times, while smart fans have grown fourfold. Indian smart fan maker Atomberg has reported a fivefold increase in sales during the festive period. Connected lighting products from brands including Philips and Wipro are also seeing strong demand as consumers prepare their homes for Diwali celebrations.Premium appliances and financing options fuel upgradesAmazon said customers are increasingly upgrading to premium and energy-efficient appliances rather than simply replacing existing products. Home appliance sales have grown 25 times during the early stages of the festival sale. Washer-dryers are growing at 18 times their average pace, while premium front-load washing machines continue to gain popularity. LG emerged as the best-selling washing machine brand, recording 17 times its regular-day sales.Air conditioners with four-star and five-star energy ratings are also witnessing strong adoption, growing 15 times faster than normal sales levels. Brands such as Panasonic, Hitachi and Daikin are among the leading sellers in the category. The company said financing options, including exchange discounts, instant bank offers and no-cost EMI plans starting at ₹99 per day, are helping drive the premiumisation trend.Small businesses boomAmazon said in a statement, "The strong festive demand for home and lifestyle products is also translating into significant momentum for small and medium businesses selling on Amazon. During the first week of the Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026, overall seller sales grew 3.5X compared to business as usual, while products sold more than twice as fast. The festival saw Amazon’s highest-ever seller participation, up nearly 30% year-on-year, with more than 70% of participating businesses coming from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Among the top-selling categories for sellers were major appliances, wireless, jewellery, shoes and automotive, reflecting the broad-based nature of festive demand and the growing opportunity for businesses beyond India’s major metros."AI tools helping customers discover productsAmazon said more than six million customers have used its Deal Alerts feature, which allows shoppers to track prices and receive notifications when products reach preferred price points. The company has also expanded AI-powered shopping tools, including Rufus, Lens AI, AI Review Highlights, Quick View, Buying Guides and personalised product recommendations, to simplify product discovery and comparison.Festival offers continue through DiwaliThe Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 sale will continue throughout the festive season, with the company offering discounts of up to 50% on more than one lakh products and its lowest prices of the year on over two lakh products across categories including Home, Kitchen, Toys and Outdoors. Customers can also avail a 10% instant discount on purchases made using Axis Bank and ICICI Bank credit cards and EMI transactions, along with additional benefits for Prime members and Amazon Pay users.
Article Summary: Growth is increasingly being driven by smaller cities, with non-metro markets accounting for more than 60% of shopping volumes. Cities such as Lucknow, Jaipur, Patna, Guwahati, Coimbatore, Nagpur, Indore and Kochi are leading demand.

Article Title: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby is very happy with airlines deal with Starlink, says helping us get customers; Elon Musk responds
Article Text:
Elon Musk Starlink

Elon Musk: 'Starlink moves the needle'

Earnings miss amid higher fuel costs

Ongoing debate with Delta Air Lines

Scott Kirby, the CEO of United Airlines is already noticing customers switch from rival carriers because of its partnership with Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX. According to the remarks made during a CNBC interview and the company's latest earnings discussion, the airline views the rollout as a key competitive advantage. Kirby highlighted that the carrier is expected to cross the milestone of having Starlink installed on more than 50% of its flights this week and that the entire fleet is expected to be equipped with the service by the end of next year, according to a Benzinga report citing the interview. "We already see customers moving from other airlines today," Kirby said when discussing the impact of the onboard internet service. However, he added that it remains unclear whether the benefit will be large enough on its own to help deliver double-digit profit margins.Kirby's comments quickly drew a response from Musk on X. Replying to a post that highlighted the interview, the billionaire wrote: "Starlink moves the needle." The exchange adds to Musk's long-running efforts to promote Starlink's aviation offering as a key differentiator for airlines seeking to improve onboard connectivity. United Airlines calls Starlink a 'tailwind'Speaking during the airline's earnings call, Kirby described Starlink as a "tailwind" for the company and said United has launched a tracking tool that allows passengers to check whether their upcoming flight is equipped with the service.Kirby also expressed confidence that the airline is building a significant lead over competitors."We're on our way to being the only global U.S. airline with Starlink at scale. A lot of new customers are going to try us. It's a huge head start," he said, according to the Benzinga report. The comments suggest that United views onboard connectivity as more than just a passenger convenience feature, seeing it instead as a tool for attracting and retaining travellers.The remarks came as United reported quarterly earnings that fell slightly short of Wall Street expectations. The airline posted earnings of $2.54 per share, below analyst estimates of $2.59 per share. Revenue of $17.875 billion also narrowly missed the consensus forecast of $17.888 billion.United said fuel expenses rose by $1.8 billion year-over-year, driven largely by energy market disruptions linked to the Iran war. During the earnings call, Kirby warned that elevated oil prices could continue to pressure the airline industry over the next year.He also said that between six and 10 U.S. airlines could lose money this year if fuel costs remain high and geopolitical tensions continue to affect energy markets.The latest comments come against the backdrop of an ongoing debate between Musk and Delta Air Lines over inflight internet connectivity. Delta has chosen to deploy Amazon's Project Kuiper-based internet service on its aircraft instead of Starlink. Musk has repeatedly criticised the decision, arguing that airlines risk losing customers by not adopting Starlink's network.In previous comments, Musk warned that Delta could lose passengers because of its decision and even mocked the carrier's onboard connectivity, claiming a flight without reliable internet would be an ideal place to isolate an AI model from online access.With United now publicly stating that Starlink is already helping attract customers from competing airlines, the debate over satellite-powered inflight internet appears set to intensify.
Article Summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby says Starlink is already helping attract customers from rival carriers. Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, is expected to be installed on more than 50% of the airline's flights this week. Kirby's comments quickly drew a response from Musk on X.

Article Title: PHP2Shell: Governments on high alert over critical website flaw; Wikipedia, hospitals, school portals go dark; what users should know
Article Text:
PHP2Shell: AI finds decade-old flaw in software behind 70% of websites; governments take sites offline

PHP is the hidden software behind most websites on the internet

The PHP2Shell flaw lets hackers take over a website without a password

AI found a flaw that had been hiding for over a decade

Most users on the internet can relax, but website owners need to update right away

A large chunk of the internet went offline on Wednesday, and most of it was switched off on purpose. Government websites in the Netherlands, Finland, France and Denmark, along with universities, hospitals and sites as big as Wikipedia, pulled systems down after two serious security flaws were found in PHP. Most people have never heard of PHP, but it is the software running behind roughly 70% of all websites, from news sites and online shops to personal blogs.The flaws, now nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a hacker take over the computer that runs a website without needing a password. They had been hiding in PHP's code for more than a decade, and it took artificial intelligence (AI) to find them. PHP's developers released a fix on October 21, but hackers moved within hours to attack websites that hadn't updated yet. Cyber security agencies in the US and the UK have told website owners to install the fix right away or take their sites offline until they can.The list of affected sites shows how far PHP reaches. The Dutch government's own cyber security agency shut its website as a precaution. Finland took several government online services offline, France's Interior Ministry put all its websites into maintenance mode, and Denmark shut its national school communication platform.In the Netherlands, the Port of Rotterdam, the national football association, several hospitals and the five largest political parties also took their sites down. The Internet Archive went offline briefly, and online forums 4chan and DeviantArt ran into trouble. Even Pokémon Home and Pokémon Champions were taken offline.Some world leaders got involved too. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi posted on X: "We have an urgent request for everyone to take action tonight."The rush makes sense once you see how fast hackers moved. Cloudflare, a company that sits in front of millions of websites to protect them, saw thousands of hacking attempts even before the flaws were made public. CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X that this climbed to tens of thousands within 45 minutes of the announcement, hundreds of thousands within two hours, and millions by the next morning.Think of a website as having two sides. The side you see is the page in your browser. The side you don't see is a computer, called a server, that builds that page every time you open it. It fetches the right text, images, prices or comments from a database and sends the finished page to your screen. PHP is the language that does this job for a huge share of the web.It has been around since the early 1990s, and it powers WordPress, the tool behind millions of blogs and business websites. It also runs Wikipedia, many government portals, and platforms like Drupal and Joomla that big organisations use to manage their websites. Web tracking firm W3Techs estimates PHP is used by about 69.3% of all websites whose underlying software it can identify.That is why a single flaw in PHP turned into a global problem. Tiffany Farriss, who heads the Drupal Association, told Reuters that any server running a version of PHP from the last 20 years would be vulnerable. "This issue impacts the majority of the internet," she said.PHP is also free and open source, which means anyone can use it. It is looked after by a small non-profit, the PHP Foundation, which has just 13 full-time and part-time engineers maintaining software that much of the internet depends on.Normally, to change a website or access its stored data, you need an administrator login. PHP2Shell skips that step entirely.The two flaws, officially tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are both rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity. In simple terms, a hacker can send a website a carefully crafted request that makes PHP run out of memory and stop halfway through its work. That leaves behind some leftover data in the server. The hacker then sends a second request that makes PHP use that leftover data as if it were normal, and that opens the door to running their own commands on the server.Once inside, a hacker can change what a website shows, plant malicious software that infects visitors, or steal what the server stores. That can include usernames and passwords, digital keys that connect the site to other services, and databases with personal information. A second route even lets hackers peek into the server's short-term memory, where they could catch passwords and login details of other people using the site at the same time.Wiz, one of the firms that found the flaws, showed working attacks on fresh WordPress, Drupal and Joomla websites. It also pointed out that the problem is in PHP itself, so even a basic website with nothing complicated on it can be at risk. Every version of PHP going back more than a decade is affected.The bugs were found by two security firms working separately. Calif says it spotted them on August 1 with the help of an AI model, which OpenAI says was its GPT-5.6 Sol. Wiz found them on August 19 using its own AI tool along with Google's Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol.What stands out is that the flaws were not new. PHP's own developers had considered a possible attack along these lines in 2024, but nobody could work out how to make it happen. According to Wiz, turning these bugs into a real attack required so many complex steps that it was at the edge of what human experts could manage. With AI, a single researcher did in a week what would earlier have taken a top team months.The plan was to keep the flaws secret until October 22, giving website companies time to prepare fixes quietly. That plan fell apart when details leaked on online forums and social media on Tuesday. PHP rushed its fix out nearly a day early. Amazon later said its systems saw a hacking attempt on October 17, four days before the public announcement, and nobody yet knows how that attacker found out.OpenAI said in a blog post that the episode shows how AI can uncover security flaws, but also how it can help attackers "rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits." The same kind of AI that found the bug can help hackers study the fix and build an attack in very little time. That is why the window between a fix coming out and attacks starting has shrunk from days to minutes.If you only browse the web, there isn't much you need to do. The flaw targets the servers that run websites, not your phone or laptop. Still, a hacked website can be used to spread malware or steal data, so stay alert for a few weeks. If a service you use asks you to change your password, do it through the official app or website. Be careful with emails or messages about the PHP flaw that ask you to click links or share details, as scammers often use big news like this as bait.If you run a website, even a small blog, check whether it uses PHP. Sites built on Squarespace or Wix are safe, as those platforms don't use PHP. Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, says websites it hosts directly, along with Tumblr, are safe. If you installed WordPress yourself or use a hosting company like GoDaddy, Bluehost or Hostinger, contact your provider to find out when the fix will reach your site.The fixed versions of PHP are 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Websites running PHP 8.1 or older won't get a fix at all, because those versions are no longer supported, so they need to move to a newer version. If your site stores customer details or takes payments and you can't confirm it has been fixed, taking it offline for a few hours is the safer choice. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre has also asked organisations that couldn't update quickly to check whether hackers have already left a hidden way back into their systems.Small websites run by individuals and small businesses are the most at risk, since they often lack a technical team and depend on their hosting company to apply fixes.Sigi Goode, a professor of information systems at the Australian National University, told The Guardian where the real danger lies. "The bigger concern is the websites that are not down today," he said. The websites that went dark on Wednesday were the ones taking the threat seriously. The ones still online without the fix are what hackers will be hunting for in the weeks ahead.
Article Summary: Government websites in the Netherlands, Finland, France and Denmark, along with universities, hospitals and sites as big as Wikipedia, pulled systems down. The flaws, now nicknamed PHP2Shell, let a hacker take over the computer that runs a website without needing a password. They had been hiding in PHP's code for more than a decade, and it took artificial intelligence (AI) to find them.

Article Title: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal shares an update on Temple device, writes ‘Temple Batch 01 pre orders open …’
Article Text:
Deepinder Goyal has announced six color options for Temple, his upcoming health wearable device

Hand-made units, three-month delivery timeline

What Temple does

The road to launch

Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has shared a new update on Temple, the hardware venture he has been teasing in recent months, announcing that pre-orders for the first batch of the device will open on November 1. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Goyal wrote, “The wait is over. Temple Batch 01 pre orders open November 1. Each @temple is hand-made to order and delivered to you within three months of your purchase." Along with announcing the pre-order date, Goyal also indicated that the company is taking a measured approach to scaling production. According to Goyal, Temple is following a "grow slow" strategy, with a focus on maintaining quality control and ensuring customers receive a strong experience. "Quality control, and also making sure we serve each customer well. Following the 'grow slow' approach with temple," Goyal said while explaining the company's approach to fulfilling orders.The latest update suggests that Temple's first production batch will be manufactured to order rather than mass-produced. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries expected within three months of purchase.The announcement gives potential buyers their first clear timeline for ordering the device, while also signalling that availability may remain limited during the initial phase as the company prioritises production quality over rapid expansion.It will come in six colours, with Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk marked as limited editions. Temple has not yet announced pricing, the number of devices in the first batch, or the exact date deliveries will begin, and said it would share more information before pre-orders open.Temple is an experimental health-tech wearable developed under a private initiative backed by Goyal. It uses optical sensors to track changes in cerebral blood flow, a metric the company calls BrainFlow. The device tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain. The wearable first drew attention when Goyal appeared on a podcast in early 2026 wearing a small metallic clip-like device on his head.In May, Goyal announced that the first 100 devices were ready to ship to select founding users, including athletes, scientists, doctors, founders and creators. In August, he said the latest version was less than half the size of the one shown earlier, and claimed it was the smallest wearable on the market by volume and the most powerful. Independent reports noted that he gave no hardware specifications or performance data to back that claim. At that time, he said the limited launch edition would ship before the end of 2026. The new three-month delivery window suggests that orders placed from November 1 could reach customers in early 2027.
Article Summary: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has announced pre-orders for Temple will open on November 1. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries expected within three months of purchase. Temple is an experimental health-tech wearable developed under a private initiative backed by Goyal.

Article Title: UltraProlink launches Juice-Up Mag 7 magnetic wireless power bank in India at Rs 3,499
Article Text: Consumer technology accessories brand UltraProlink has expanded its portable charging portfolio with the launch of the Juice-Up Mag 7, a 10,000mAh magnetic wireless power bank designed for smartphones and other compatible devices. The new power bank combines magnetic wireless charging and wired fast charging in a slim 16.5mm form factor. According to the company, the Juice-Up Mag 7 supports up to 15W magnetic wireless charging, 22.5W USB-C Power Delivery (PD) output and 22W PPS fast charging. The product is aimed at users looking for a travel-friendly charging solution for daily commutes, work and travel.The Juice-Up Mag 7 offers magnetic wireless charging with support for 5W, 7.5W, 10W and 15W charging speeds, depending on the connected device. UltraProlink said the magnetic alignment system is designed to work with compatible smartphones, including supported iPhone, Pixel, Samsung and OnePlus devices. For users seeking faster charging speeds, the power bank also supports up to 22.5W USB-C PD charging. The company claims compatible iPhone models can charge from 0% to 50% in 30 minutes through the USB-C port, although actual performance may vary depending on device, battery condition and usage.The device supports multiple charging standards, including PD 3.0, PD 2.0, PPS, QC 3.0, QC 2.0, AFC, PE 2.0, PE 1.1 and SCP, enabling compatibility across a wide range of smartphones and gadgets.Despite housing a 10,000mAh battery, UltraProlink says the Juice-Up Mag 7 measures just 16.5mm thick, making it suitable for carrying in backpacks, laptop bags and travel pouches. The power bank features an integrated LCD display that shows the remaining battery percentage, allowing users to monitor available charge at a glance. The company also highlighted that the 38.5Wh battery capacity meets flight-safe requirements, making it suitable for air travel.UltraProlink said the power bank is BIS certified and manufactured in India. It also incorporates the company's Safety Shield protection system, which includes safeguards against short circuits, overheating, overcurrent and overcharging.The UltraProlink Juice-Up Mag 7 10,000mAh portable power bank is priced at Rs 3,499 and is available through UltraProlink.com and Amazon.in.
Article Summary: The Juice-Up Mag 7 combines magnetic wireless charging and wired fast charging in a slim 16.5mm form factor. The product is aimed at users looking for a travel-friendly charging solution for daily commutes, work and travel. UltraProlink said the magnetic alignment system is designed to work with compatible smartphones, including supported iPhone, Pixel and Samsung devices.
